newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Direct Taiwan-China ship link set for April - paper.
newsitem.headline: Direct Taiwan-China ship link set for April - paper.

text.p: Ships will start sailing directly between Taiwan and the Chinese mainland in early April, ending Taiwan's nearly five-decade-old ban on such links, the Commercial Times and Economic Daily News reported on Thursday.

The Commercial Times quoted unidentified sources as saying many Taiwan shipping industry leaders had received invitations for an April 8 ceremony in China's southeastern port of Xiamen to mark the first direct sailing.
Government officials were not available for immediate comment.
Yang Ming Marine, Uniglory Marine and Wan Hai Lines are among several Taiwan shippers that have applied to mainland officials for permission to sail across the strait.

The Economic Daily News confirmed that China had begun to process the shippers' applications and quoted unidentified Ministry of Transportation and Communication sources as saying "the first good news could be near."
Any crossings would involve Taiwan's southern port of Kaohsiung, the reports said. Officials have said service could eventually be expanded to the west coast port of Taichung.

Xiamen is a flourishing trade gateway and special economic zone in China's Fujian province, which hosts billions of dollars in Taiwan investment, and lies closer to Kaohsiung than any other mainland port.
The Commercial Times said the Fujian capital of Fuzhou just northeast from Xiamen was being considered as a second port to pioneer direct links.

Taiwan and China have been divided since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949, when the Nationalist Chinese government, defeated by the communists, took refuge on the island. Taipei has banned all official contacts ever since.
